reviews.text: Assessed on a level of tone and aesthetic, Villeneuve’s film is a stunning work. It is oppressive and unsettling, achieving Lynchian levels of discomfort and uncertainty.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Enemy is brimming with non-commercial bravado that borders on being confessional. Just as Hitchcock made manifest his voyeuristic and controlling proclivities, Villeneuve exposes his own conflicted feelings towards women and monogamy.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: It will haunt the shit out of you
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: It's a thought-provoking film that plays on the mind for days afterwards.
reviews.author: Nick Levine

reviews.text: A stylish and sinister (with a big tasty dollop of mystery on the side) that will keep audiences guessing long after they've left the theatre.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Perhaps more important than the conundrum at the heart of the film is the skillfully crafted feeling of perplexity.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal meets his doppelgänger - or maybe it's also him - and mostly they argue...
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: It's a beautiful, nightmarishly warped universe ripe for multiple readings and psychological explanations concerning hidden desires and oppositions.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Enemy is the type of film you just can't shake.
reviews.author: Josh Goller

reviews.text: Whilst the mysterious premise and sensory illusions make for a relatively mesmeric experience, Villeneuve struggles to repress the same heavy-handedness that's been present throughout his oeuvre.
reviews.author: Patrick Gamble

reviews.text: Enemy wants so much to be profound and provocative that it fails to ground itself in any way.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: This movie took a lot out of me last night.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: I'm a huge fan of Villeneuve and Gyllenhall, but this is just not a good movie.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: I liked Enemy a lot. I see so many movies each year, many of which are near-clones of previous movies, that it's a treat to see a movie with an unconventional take on things, even if it's disturbing.
reviews.author: Marcianne Miller

reviews.text: If "Enemy" is the weakest of the three Villeneuve films I've seen, the problem is its reliance on gratuitous weirdness to do its heavy lifting.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: While the film is finely crafted and boasts excellent performances from female leads Laurent and Sarah Gadon, everything is too restrained and tasteful and, in particular, too reliant on the suspense trope of the chase.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: It's all style - and what wonderful, skillful style it is - with little substance.
reviews.author: Alex Heeney

reviews.text: Featuring a tremendous performance by Jake Gyllenhaal and bold direction from Denis Villeneuve, Enemy is a masterfully crafted film with a tricky but very fulfilling premise.
reviews.author: Jay Ledbetter

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal embodies both men with care, building distinct characters that no amount of physical similarity can prevent discerning who is who.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: For those who enjoy a different kind of cinema, this is not to be missed.
reviews.author: Emine Yildirim

reviews.text: As with many Gyllenhaal flicks, a huge amount goes unsaid - such as what is going on.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: From the opening shot of Enemy, you are trained to expect something out of the ordinary.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Rewarding for those who enjoy the menace and mystery that accompanies the cinema of the mind.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: The eerie music and abstract, experimental approach to storytelling creates a disquieting ambiance which emanates off the screen, turning what could effectively be a light tale, into something that seems so sinister.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: Villeneuve knows how to stoke the tension so that benign moments become first unsettling and then downright creepy.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: This may be a thriller starring Jake Gyllenhaal, but mainstream audiences should also note that this is an artful film that refuses to tell its story using the usual formula.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: As Adam pursues his doppelganger across a Toronto of sleek, soulless high-rises, director Denis Villeneuve throws in puzzlingly surreal touches ... What on earth - or, more likely, the subconscious - is going on?
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal faces the tricky task of conveying the subtle differences of two men whose identities are thrown into flux. The result is his most nuanced performance since playing another sleuth caught out of his depth in Zodiac.
reviews.author: Jason Anderson

reviews.text: This is a thematically rich psychological thriller which examines identity, responsibility and desire and sets out to disorientate and perplex.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: Enemy has morbid elegance to spare, which should guarantee it some long-term cult prestige.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: For all its allusions to totalitarianism and the concept of selfhood, this tale of a lecturer who encounters his exact double lacks depth and meaning.
reviews.author: Lewis Porteous

reviews.text: Enemy asks questions of its viewer, but by the time it's all over - closing with one of the most infuriating final scenes in recent memory - the will to answer them may not be present.
reviews.author: Simon Reynolds

reviews.text: This could be Villeneuve's most accomplished film so far.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The doppelgänger trope may sound well worn but Enemy finds fresh, deeply unnerving ground. And Jake Gyllenhaal gives two spellbinding performances.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Lots of good stuff here, precious little of which has any lasting impact.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal gives not one magnetic, alert yet opaque performance here. He gives two.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: A weird, intriguing tchotchke of a thriller ...
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Heavy with symbolism and the subconscious, Villeneuve's remote style, de-saturated palate and lack of answers make Enemy difficult to love, but it will stay with you.
reviews.author: Andrew Collins

reviews.text: A powerful and challenging film with a great deal of psychological symbolism. If it's a hallucination or alternate universe experience is up to you.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: One could go back for a second (and, probably, third) viewing to try to put the film together, but it's doubtful they'd have any desire to.
reviews.author: Zach Hollwedel

reviews.text: In one of the most striking and perplexing final scenes of a film in recent memory, Villeneuve's Enemy is at its most enigmatic.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: It has the feeling of a film not thought about all the way through, one that seems as though it was improvised scene by scene. There was certainly the start of a good idea in here, it's just a shame that we don't get to see it come to life.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Apreciar um filme apenas como experiência narrativa ou pela força de suas atuações não é proibido - e explorar seus temas após a sessão é um esforço intelectual que pode ser imensamente divertido em vez de frustrante.
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Enemy lets its audience put the dots together, but every single one of those dots have been completely thought out by Villeneuve and all involved.
reviews.author: Jack Giroux

reviews.text: An eerie doppelganger drama
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: I can't get Enemy's peculiar, fevered mood, or the memory of that wackadoo last image, out of my head.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Challenging "Enemy" Refuses to Pander
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Among all the movies out there about seeing double, this one feels genuinely singular.
reviews.author: José Teodoro

reviews.text: Fascinating and frustrating, viewers may find more 'undeciphered' than 'order' in its resolution.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: A mismatch of ideas OR a brilliant "art house experiment." It may take me a few years to decide which.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: There's some pleasure to be had in the contrast between the grubby worldliness of Villeneuve's mise en scene ... and the trajectory of Saramago's doppelgangers.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: If their previous collaboration, "Prisoners," was a major-label studio album, than "Enemy" is the EP put out on their own label - rougher, less conventionally satisfying, but with a nervy spirit all its own.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Enemy presents a real puzzle. In fact, it's so elegantly done at times that you don't even realize you're in a puzzle
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: A feat of sustained tension and unrelieved dread that spins its web of unease with elegantly creepy visuals (the Toronto sky seems dusted with noxious yellow pollen) and spooky sound design (the score consists of nervous strings and sonorous woodwinds).
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: A spooky enigma, more ponderous than provocative, more silly than suspenseful.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: The story itself is fascinating, the score is tense and edgy, and the cinematography paints Toronto as a skewed city of angles and facades.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: A nifty bit of murky fun rife with unsettling imagery and a sense of taut dread even Alfred Hitchcock would have admired.
reviews.author: Ryan Lattanzio

reviews.text: Despite some flaws and frustrations, this is one movie whose ending you will not see coming.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: ... a compelling and head-scratching exploration of obsession and paranoia that leaves plenty of angles for post-film chatter.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Is it creepy? Yes. Is it puzzling? Yes. Is it disturbing? Yes. Will it appeal to you? That's a hard call, but it will have an appeal to those looking for something out of the ordinary.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is impressive in a weirdly original thriller from Villeneuve that trips over its many legs at the finish.
reviews.author: Jeff Baker

reviews.text: A woozy, danger-infused rumination on identity that triggers tripwires of panic and sexual compulsion, Enemy is like a cold glass of water to the face of cinematic formalism.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: Ambiguous to a fault, it's at least unique and challenging, and in a season largely dominated by imbecilic efforts like Need for Speed and Pompeii -- films that go out of their way to kill precious brain cells -- that certainly counts for something.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Attempts to draw out a thin story that doesn't support incessant delay. The movie is frustratingly tedious at times, mistaking stillness for mounting suspense.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Movies about doubles are, almost by definition, creepy, but Villeneuve, not to be outdone, piles on the weirdness.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Captivating adaptation of José Saramago's novel, The Double.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: I wish I had found the meaning of "Enemy" or could have enjoyed it, but I wish I could get my time back.
reviews.author: Jolene Mendez

reviews.text: "Enemy" is what might happen if someone let Terrence Malick make a "Twilight Zone" episode, with a quick rewrite by David Cronenberg.
reviews.author: Peter Hartlaub

reviews.text: Despite Gyllenhaal's twitchy, two-headed performance, "Enemy" is hobbled by a genetic flaw: Suspension of disbelief has a twin called suspicion of dumbness.
reviews.author: Joe Williams

reviews.text: Denis Villeneuve's moody, intriguing and, yes, occasionally silly psychological thriller.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The story's dour flatness keeps it from being as disturbing as it aims to be.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: The wan, lifeless palette matches the film's overarching tone of drained, depressive enervation.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: "Enemy" may be built more on questions than answers, but in the probing it generates a satisfyingly arch hum of weirdness.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: A bravely imaginative, startlingly unnerving, freakily mesmerizing puzzle-box mindbender.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: This is fitfully successful as a mood piece, though the dream imagery is heavy-handed, the characters sketchily realized, and the high-toned dialogue comes out stilted more often than not.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: A practical joke posing as a brain teaser.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Watching "Enemy," in which Gyllenhaal cleverly delineates the character differences and confidence levels of the two leading roles, it's clear that the movie is messing with you, in a highly calibrated fashion.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Not just dark but dank, Denis Villeneuve's "Enemy" is a surpassingly creepy film about identity.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: "Enemy" is quietly and effectively eerie except when it's idiotic. Oh, well.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: ...takes a simple, familiar premise and overloads it with atmospheric and existential import.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Enemy feels quite distinctly as a mood piece, a ring of swirling colours and emotions that seems more intent on leaving a mental mark or scar on the viewer than anything resembling a sense of narrative fulfillment.
reviews.author: Glenn Dunks

reviews.text: The movie sticks to you ... and the ending is strange and sudden enough to make you revise, or interrogate, all that has come before.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: We can't help but refuse to ignore the experience, digging deeper and deeper into the horrors that await us.
reviews.author: Christopher Runyon

reviews.text: Enemy thinks it's shattering your brain. All it's really doing is squashing women under the blocky pretense of one self-centered man.
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal sheds any hints of movie star vanity to indulge in this mysterious existential descent into madness.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: Like a David Lynch film, with clues, emotions, images, ideas, and sensations coming together for one unique experience, with a bizarre, unforgettable ending.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: ...a brilliantly complex thriller that does not let the viewer relax one iota.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Villeneuve is a very self-conscious artist whose estimable work descends from the European high-modernist tradition of decades past.
reviews.author: Godfrey Cheshire

reviews.text: Villeneuve throws meaty clues for us chew on, his direction amplifying the thematic boil while keeping us on the edge of our seats.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: Enemy operates on a level of carefully calibrated unease, where the very elusiveness of motivation and logic is exploited for purposes of sustained cinematic disorientation.
reviews.author: Geoff Pevere

reviews.text: Enemy slowly but surely envelops us, like the web of the spider that seems to be crawling from Adam's psyche right into the real world.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal masters the Jekyll and Hyde side of the job by finding the right dynamic with his foil.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal does an excellent job creating two very different personas for the story. But this means that when the cards are down, all Enemy has in its hand is a single pair.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: There is only so much sense a movie like this needs to make, and this one succeeds in being divertingly clever and effectively creepy.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: As the questions mount and the plot's twists get more and more improbable, the director's fierce control and fine-grained technique grow all the more impressive.
reviews.author: Trey Graham

reviews.text: Between Gyllenhaal's two characters and their two solitudes, Villeneuve creates some delicious tension, laced with humour, and a sense of latent menace that draws us into a web with no exit.
reviews.author: Brian D. Johnson

reviews.text: The saving grace of this tricky, unsettling movie is Jake Gyllenhaal's edgy turn. Or, rather, his two edgy turns.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: It doesn't add up to much of anything exciting ...
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: Where ['Prisoners'] got worse as it got sillier, 'Enemy' gets better when [director Denis] Villeneuve starts having fun.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is eloquently subtle, but this muddled identity-thriller relies on misdirection and leaves you feeling not stunned, just cheated.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: This puzzling new addition to the doppleganger genre never finds its footing.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: Even with a final third that doesn't deliver on the setup, the movie more than makes it across the finish line.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: The movie is too literal and compartmentalized to take the psychological plunge it seems to constantly be intimating.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: Gloriously enigmatic.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: Jake Gyllenhaal embodies the two roles with real presence, establishing Adam's sniveling wimp and Anthony's striding jerk as two believably discrete sides of the same coin.
reviews.author: Jesse Cataldo

reviews.text: ...provides few answers to its central mystery but beguiles via a mood of oppressive existential dread.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: A great exercise in unconventional film making, and it left me thinking about it long after the film was over.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: The end resolution had a cramped quality that I'm still not sure what to make of, but then again it means that "Enemy" is a unique film experience that will be fun to sort out once you've gone through it for yourself.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: The sinister and devious Enemy is an epic mind-screw that crawls around in the dark corners of the psyche like a spider in a dusty attic.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Enemy is a mysterious and strangely atmospheric thriller, but outside of an exceptional dual performance by Jake Gyllenhaal, its enigmatic and nonsensical nature offer very little reason to watch.
reviews.author: David Baldwin

reviews.text: ...it's hard to deny that the film, which boasts an impressively memorable final few minutes, lingers in one's consciousness long after the end credits have rolled.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Mysterious enough that many viewers will insist on seeing it twice.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: A highly stylized yet intriguing look at a man coming to terms with his duplicate...Enemy firmly establishes Villeneuve as one of today's most truly unique filmmakers.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: With Enemy, Denis Villeneuve confidently proves he's contemporary filmmaking's ultimate troll.
reviews.author: Tina Hassannia

reviews.text: I kinda dug it but I have no idea if it's any good or what happened or where I am anymore and what aiiiiiiiieeeeeeee that last sound/shot. WTF
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: A slow-burning metaphysical thriller that stays one step ahead of its audience.
reviews.author: Anthony Kaufman

reviews.text: As hauntingly strange as it is inconclusive and frustrating, Enemy, directed by Denis Villeneuve (Incendies), is one of the more head-scratching additions to the doppelganger genre. Yet it will certainly have its fans.
reviews.author: Deborah Young

reviews.text: Might have the scariest ending of any film ever made.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Thick with weighty themes, disquieting portent and anxious tension, Villeneuve...crafts a gripping slow burn portrait of the male id/ego, our self-destructive tendencies and how they control us.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

synopsis: A mild-mannered college professor (Jake Gyllenhaal) discovers a look-alike actor and delves into the other man's private affairs.
